replacements.proposed_text: Fossé traversant un étang et aboutissant à sa bonde (nom masculin ; emploi de drainage, caractère quotidien non établi).
replacements.accepted_text: Fossé traversant un étang et aboutissant à sa bonde (nom masculin ; géographie, drainage d’un étang).

exact_source.reviewed_excerpt: # [[fossé|Fossé]] qui traverse un [[étang]], aboutissant à sa [[bonde]].

replacements.review_reason: The fixed line and original 1827 scan both identify a ditch through a pond to its bonde. Retain that wording and masculine gender; the current publisher’s Geography label scopes the use. Contemporary maintenance evidence resolves the editorial everyday gap.

replacements.proposed_text: A ditch crossing a pond and ending at its outlet sluice (masculine French noun; drainage use, everyday status not established).
replacements.accepted_text: A ditch crossing a pond and ending at its drain outlet (masculine French noun; geography, pond drainage).

exact_source.reviewed_excerpt: # [[fossé|Fossé]] qui traverse un [[étang]], aboutissant à sa [[bonde]].

replacements.review_reason: Drain outlet matches bonde without requiring a sluice mechanism. Pond geography restricts this French noun and excludes English by; current usage corroboration supplies no bundled wording.

replacements.proposed_text: 穿过池塘并通向其排水闸的沟渠（法语阳性名词；排水用语，尚未确立其日常用法）。
replacements.accepted_text: 穿过池塘并通向其排水口的沟渠（法语阳性名词；地理用语，池塘排水）。

exact_source.reviewed_excerpt: # [[fossé|Fossé]] qui traverse un [[étang]], aboutissant à sa [[bonde]].

replacements.review_reason: 排水口 identifies the outlet without inventing a gate. 穿过池塘、沟渠 and 地理用语 preserve the fixed meaning and masculine French noun; the contemporary use supports removal of the unresolved-status phrase.

usage_changes.proposed_usage: French pond-drainage noun; retained proposal with unresolved modern everyday eligibility.
usage_changes.accepted_usage: French masculine noun for a pond drainage ditch leading to its drain outlet; geography and routine pond maintenance.
usage_changes.reason: The publisher’s current French masculine-noun entry labels Geography, supplies a blocked-drain situation involving plastic bags, and dates its update 11/03/26. Clearing a pond drainage ditch is a routine concrete maintenance activity. This is sufficient modern everyday semantic evidence under the ticket, which has no commonness/frequency threshold; retain the pond-drainage restriction. The example is dictionary usage evidence, not measured corpus frequency or a claim of widespread use. No owner exception is involved.
